At Ripple, we’re building a world where value moves like information does today. It’s big, it’s bold, and we’re already doing it. Through our crypto solutions for financial institutions, businesses, governments and developers, we are improving the global financial system and creating greater economic fairness and opportunity for more people, in more places around the world. And we get to do the best work of our career and grow our skills surrounded by colleagues who have our backs. 

If you’re ready to see your impact and unlock incredible career growth opportunities, join us, and build real world value.

THE WORK:

  • The position offers a commercially-minded finance lawyer the opportunity to be part of the Ripple Legal team supporting the US business of its Ripple Prime product offering, such as its equity products, including cash equities prime brokerage, together with derivatives, securities lending, repo and related financing products. The role will also have exposure to futures and options, fixed income, FX and digital assets.
  • Provide legal support and advise across Ripple's regulated and unregulated entities for Ripple Prime products.
  • Interact with Product, Sales, Trading, Credit, Risk, Compliance, Operations and other front- and back-office functions, as well as external legal advisers.
  • This is a technically challenging and highly rewarding role offering significant responsibility, continuous professional development and collaboration with colleagues across Ripple!

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Act as a key legal adviser for US equity products, including Ripple's cash equities prime brokerage framework covering margin financing, short selling, securities lending and borrowing, custody, clearing and settlement, and executing broker arrangements.
  • Draft, structure and negotiate client, counterparty and financing documentation, such as prime brokerage, margin and account agreements, ISDA Master Agreements and CSAs, securities lending agreements (MSLAs and GMSLAs) and repurchase agreements (MRAs and GMRAs), as well as MCAs, futures agreements and debt agreements where required.
  • Advise on OTC derivatives offered alongside the prime brokerage business, including equity total return and portfolio swaps and options, together with related confirmations and collateral arrangements.
  • Provide legal review and approval for new products, markets, jurisdictions and innovative transaction structures.
  • Support Ripple’s regulated entities, including its broker-dealer, swap dealer and futures commission merchant, in relation to applicable SEC, FINRA, CFTC, NFA and exchange requirements, including margin, short sale, customer protection and securities lending requirements.
  • Develop and maintain legal templates, negotiation playbooks and scalable contracting processes.
  • Manage competing priorities, including urgent and time-sensitive matters, while providing clear and practical advice with minimal supervision.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • General financial law and experience, with an emphasis on prime brokerage (ideally US equity prime brokerage), securities financing, derivatives or capital markets. Experience with lending arrangements and other financing transactions would be an advantage.
  • Sound knowledge of OTC derivatives and related documentation. Experience across equity, FX, index and digital asset derivatives preferred.
  • A working knowledge of the US cash equities prime brokerage model and its regulatory framework, including margin lending, short selling, securities lending and custody, and the related rules (e.g. Regulation T, Regulation SHO, SEC Rules 15c3-1 and 15c3-3 and FINRA Rule 4210).
  • Commercial awareness and good judgment are essential skills.
  • Experience gained in private practice, in-house at a financial institution, or through a combination of both.
  • Experience drafting, structuring and negotiating documentation for financial transactions, in particular prime brokerage and margin agreements, ISDA Master Agreements and CSAs (including for equity swaps, portfolio swaps and options), securities lending agreements (MSLA/GMSLA) and repurchase agreements (MRA/GMRA). Experience with futures agreements and debt agreements preferred.
  • Experience advising a prime broker, broker-dealer, investment bank or comparable financial institution preferred.
  • Some understanding of exchange-traded futures and the futures commission merchant model is helpful but is not essential.
  • Broad knowledge of financial services legal and regulatory issues. Wider experience with digital assets is helpful but not essential.
  • Excellent technical legal skills and analytical ability.
  • Strong business judgment, communication skills and commercial awareness.
  • Ability to work effectively and calmly in a fast-moving, high-volume environment.
  • JD or equivalent law degree and admission in good standing in at least one US jurisdiction. Admission in New York is preferred.
  • 5-10 years post-qualification experience for the seniority of the position would be preferable.
  • Ability to manage time effectively while working under minimal supervision.
For positions that will be based in NY, the annual salary range for this position is below. Actual salaries may vary based on numerous factors including, among other things, an individual applicant’s experience and qualifications for the position. This range does not include equity or additional compensation, such as bonuses or commissions.

$236,000—$295,000 USD

WHO WE ARE:

  • A learning environment where you can dive deep into the latest technologies and make an impact.  A professional development budget to support other modes of learning.
  • Thrive in an environment where no matter what race, ethnicity, gender, origin, or culture they identify with, every employee is a respected, valued, and empowered part of the team.

Across Wealth Management, Goldman Sachs helps empower clients and customers around the world to reach their financial goals. Our advisor-led wealth management businesses provide financial planning, investment management, banking and comprehensive advice to a wide range of clients, including ultra-high net worth and high net worth individuals, as well as family offices, foundations and endowments, and corporations and their employees. Our consumer business provides digital solutions for customers to better spend, borrow, invest, and save. Across Wealth Management, our growth is driven by a relentless focus on our people, our clients and customers, and leading-edge technology, data and design.

 

Goldman Sachs Private Bank

Goldman Sachs Private Bank provides competitive borrowing and cash management solutions from Goldman Sachs Bank USA that are strategically integrated with our client’s wealth management goals.  Our experienced team partners with PWAs to advise clients on new loans, refinancing and restructuring of existing loans along with overall liability management.  Our lenders and mortgage specialists provide a wide range of creative borrowing solutions against asset classes ranging from marketable securities and alternative investments, residential and commercial real estate to more tailored solutions against private assets such as aviation, fine art or vineyards.  All team members are employees of Goldman Sachs Bank, USA. 

###HEADING###Your Impact

The SBL and Margin Risk and Portfolio Management Associate plays a critical role in supporting the Private Bank’s credit delivery model. Working closely with Senior Underwriters, Originators, Credit Executives, Strats, Engineering and Risk partners, the Associate is responsible for designing risk methodology for lending values and initial margins, the management of the SBL and Margin portfolio and preparing underwriting analyses of portfolios of ultra‑high‑net‑worth individuals, families, and family offices.

This role blends quantitative financial analysis, credit judgment, and cross‑functional collaboration.

Key Responsibilities

Quantitative analysis and portfolio management

  • Prepare detailed analysis of financial collateral incl. Equities, Fixed Income, Structured Notes. Funds, Commodities, and exposure analysis including derivatives exposure.
  • Support ongoing portfolio monitoring, including tracking of market risk factors, scenario stress analysis, and margin call oversight.

Methodology

  • Partner with Strats, Engineering and Business Stakeholders to develop loan-to-value methodology for financial collateral and initial margin methodology for derivatives.

  • Provide theoretical and empirical analysis to support model development and ensure proper governance throughout the model development process. 

Risk & Governance

  • Identify data gaps or potential risk issues and escalate appropriately.

Qualifications

Required

  • 3–6 years of experience in VaR modeling for financial collateral and derivatives.
  • Strong mathematical and statistics skills.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting UHNW or institutional‑level borrowers.
  • Familiarity with SBL and Margin lending
  • CFA, FRM or similar qualifications

Success Factors

  • Strong analytical rigor and excellent logical reasoning
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with partners within the Private Bank and more broadly across Goldman Sachs.
  • Ownership mindset and accountability for quality and accuracy.
  • Professional communication and client‑focused execution.

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

 

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

The Consumer SEO & AEO team helps people discover Kraken through search engines and AI answers, understand our products and become customers. We connect content, technical SEO, international growth and automation to measurable acquisition, working with Product, Web, Engineering, Data and Compliance.

You will report to the Head of SEO & AEO and work closely with our SEO & AEO Content Lead. Together, they set priorities and provide strategy, briefs and guidance; you help turn those plans into shipped improvements across the website. Your focus is hands-on SEO/AEO delivery and always-on work, giving both leaders more capacity for GTM, strategy and content direction.

 

The opportunity

  • Own the delivery of SEO and AEO improvements across the website, helping turn the team’s strategy into live changes quickly and accurately.

  • Strong writing, editing and fact-checking skills. You can turn a brief or AI-generated draft into useful, search-optimised content that follows brand guidance. You verify product claims and incorporate detailed review feedback accurately.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The payments landscape is changing rapidly and our team is at the forefront of this change. Depending on where you live, you may be used to paying with a credit card or bank direct debit (United States), iDEAL (Netherlands) or UPI (India), amongst hundreds of other global payment methods. It turns out how you pay is increasingly dependent on where you are and what business you're buying from.
The Core Payments team makes it easy for businesses global and domestic to offer familiar local payment experiences wherever their customers choose to pay. We build bank payment methods and local payment experiences, alongside the capabilities that make these methods easier to discover, integrate, and use across Stripe. Responsible for building Stripe's payment platform that allows us to build and distribute payment methods at scale. The team works across product, engineering, design, data science, partnerships, risk, and go-to-market teams to help businesses offer locally relevant payment experiences at global scale.

What you’ll do

As a Product Manager, you’ll own relationships with some of the world’s largest payment providers and build products that drive billions in payment volume growth. You’ll help merchants offer locally relevant payment methods online and in person, improve payment performance, and expand acceptance across borders and into use cases such as recurring and agentic payments.
You’ll work directly with merchants to understand their payment needs, then partner with partnership managers and Stripe’s and financial partners’ product and engineering teams to define joint roadmaps and ship solutions. You’ll prioritize investments that grow adoption and improve approval rates while balancing revenue, margins, cost, and risk.

Responsibilities

  • Own the product vision and multi-quarter roadmap for a portfolio of strategic payment methods, using merchant feedback, partner capabilities, payment data, and market trends to set priorities.
  • Work directly with merchants and financial partners to identify gaps in payment workflows and translate them into product requirements.
  • Build joint roadmaps with partnership managers and partners’ product and engineering teams, securing alignment on investments and resolving competing priorities and dependencies.
  • Make the case for new investments and work with engineering teams to ship improvements, balancing adoption, approval rates, revenue, margins, cost, and risk.
  • Grow payment method adoption with go-to-market teams by expanding cross-border acceptance and supporting use cases such as recurring and agentic payments.
  • Partner with Risk, Legal, and Compliance to implement controls and enforcement strategies that protect Stripe and financial partners while maximizing approval rates and minimizing losses.
  • Work with product marketing and go-to-market teams to turn roadmap priorities into clear launch and adoption plans.
  • Become the product expert for your payment partners, providing insights and support to help them succeed on Stripe.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 6+ years of experience in building, launching, and scaling products that deliver meaningful user and business results.
  • Experience independently defining product strategy and executing multi-quarter roadmaps, bringing clarity and direction to ambiguous problems.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership, with the ability to influence product outcome, navigate competing interests, and drive decisions across teams and external partners.
  • Experience working on products that require aligning multiple stakeholders, developing joint roadmaps, and navigating competing priorities between internal goals and external partner objectives.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering closely with engineers, designers, and external partners to build products and complex systems at scale.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a knack for precise and concise articulation of user problems
  • Strong analytical capabilities with experience defining and tracking success metrics, running experiments (e.g., holdback tests), and using data to measure product impact on revenue, conversion, and margins.
  • Deep user empathy and sound product judgment, with experience translating complex user needs into intuitive experiences and technical capabilities.
  • Ability to thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced environment with significant autonomy and responsibility.
  • Strong business acumen and comfort with complex ecosystem and platform-level problems.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with bank payments, online, local and instore payments methods with deep understanding of the conversion, costs, and risk trade-offs.
  • Experience working with financial partners navigating risk, legal, and compliance requirements and users from various geographies and cultures.
  • Experience building platform products and driving product adoption across multiple markets.

This position can be based out of San Francisco or New York.

OVERVIEW

Modern Treasury is hiring a Product Manager to help build and grow our Payments product. Payments enables companies to move money across the world. You will own core capabilities like how businesses get onboarded, verify identity, meet compliance requirements, access payment rails, and manage liquidity over fiat and stablecoin, all through Modern Treasury. You’ll bring products to life using advanced AI tools and leading engineering and customer-facing teams.

As a Product Manager on Payments, you will work with engineering, compliance, partnerships, and customer-facing teams to ship the infrastructure that powers payments for some of the largest and fastest-growing companies in the economy. Modern Treasury is often the most critical piece of infrastructure our customers use, and the Payments product sits at the center of how money actually moves.

We are looking for someone who has built payments products before and is excited to go deep on the full lifecycle of money movement — from a customer's first onboarding moment through real-time payments at scale, across both US and international rails.

ABOUT MODERN TREASURY

Modern Treasury provides trusted infrastructure for money movement. The company helps teams launch and scale payment experiences in days, not months. With best-in-class developer tools and a single API for fiat and stablecoins—plus built-in compliance, ledgering, and reporting—Modern Treasury enables businesses to move money instantly, reliably, and at scale.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Payments Product Manager, you will own products that make up Modern Treasury's Payments offering. You will leverage AI where possible and push the envelope of what AI-enabled product execution looks like. You will be responsible for researching, designing, and delivering products related to:

  • Onboarding & Compliance: You will help manage the experience of getting customers and their end users onto the platform quickly and safely. You will design onboarding flows that reduce time-to-first-payment while meeting the requirements of banks, partners, and regulators. You will also work closely with our compliance and risk teams to translate KYC, KYB, sanctions, and other regulatory requirements into product.

  • Payment rails: You will go deep into the design of the rails that power payments — domestic schemes like ACH, wire, and RTP, international and cross-border rails, and emerging options including stablecoins. You will prioritize which rails to add and how to expose them in a unified, reliable way. You will also work with Customer Success and Support teams to ensure reliability and good support in cases of incidents.

  • Liquidity: You will help define how funds are funded, held, and moved so that customers can settle payments efficiently. You will work on the product capabilities that give customers visibility and control over balances and liquidity across accounts and rails. In this role, you’ll interface with existing bank partners and stablecoin partners, and help scale the Payments across geographies.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • AI Fluency: You will help build and run AI-native workflows across the business. This is a hands-on, business-first role: you will identify inefficiencies, scope solutions, and use the best AI tools available to create compounding leverage for the team. You do not need to train models, but you should be fluent in applying modern AI tools to real business problems.

  • Payments experience: You have built payments products before and are familiar with both US and international payments. You understand how rails work end to end and what it takes to move money reliably at scale.

  • Cross-border expertise: Ideally, you have experience with both US and international cross-border payment rails, and you understand the operational and regulatory realities of moving money across borders.

  • Interest in or experience with stablecoins: You have experience with, or a strong interest in, stablecoins. You’ve studied how they work, and have opinions about how they fit into the future of global money movement.

  • Technical fluency: You relish going deep with engineers on the details of payment systems. You are technical-literate — you can read API docs and bank or scheme specs — and you are comfortable diving into data, including SQL, while knowing when not to.

  • Customer obsession: You want to spend a ton of time with customers and prospects, understanding their business models, flows of funds, and the support they need. You can translate those needs into clear engineering requirements.

  • Ownership at scale: You have a track record of shipping and iterating on products and are comfortable with a dynamic, responsive roadmap driven by the demands of customers and partners. You can work across compliance, partnerships, sales, and customer success to deliver.

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. 

The Prime team's mission is to build Bitstamp's prime brokerage for institutional clients — the platform that lets hedge funds, market makers, and professional trading firms fund, trade, borrow against, and settle positions at scale. We build the systems that move real institutional money: cross-venue settlement, credit against collateral, matched-book lending, and the bridge that brings tokenized securities to our order book. These are correctness-critical systems where a wrong answer can't be cheaply undone — getting them right is the whole job.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer to join our team. As a Backend Engineer, you will lead the backend development process for core components and build services from inception to deployment. This individual will be helping solve correctness, scaling, and reliability challenges on a backend-first, high-performance, and world-class institutional trading platform.

This role is based in our London office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. 

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. 

Requires participation in an on-call rotation to support business needs.

What you’ll do

The Account team owns how every OKX user first gets in and keeps getting in safely. That covers registration, login and authentication, session and device management, account recovery, account security, sub-accounts and institutional accounts, and the full account lifecycle. We build the identity and access foundation that every other product depends on. That foundation has to scale to millions of users across regions and be resilient against constant attack, while still feeling easy to use. Our goal is a platform where strong security and a smooth user experience support each other rather than compete. For accounts, "mostly secure" isn't secure. Every control we build has to be consistent in how it's enforced, complete in what it covers, and explainable when it acts.

 

What You'll Be Doing

  • Formulate, select and develop technical designs across the account domain. That includes registration and onboarding, login and multi-factor authentication, passwordless login, third-party and single sign-on, session and device management, account recovery, sub-account and institutional account structures, and account lifecycle controls such as freezing, closure and data retention.
  • Build AI/ML-powered features such as account-takeover detection, suspicious-login detection, automated attack and bot defense, risk-based authentication, smarter recovery flows, and support-assist tools for account issues.
  • Organize and coordinate resources, lead research and development, troubleshoot problems, and ensure quality and on-time delivery. This includes integrating AI models into login, risk and recovery workflows.
  • Facilitate cross-team communication and promote efficient teamwork through code quality control and collaboration. This includes partnering with Security, Risk, Data Science, Compliance and Customer Support to bring models into production on reliable, auditable infrastructure.
  • Define where AI-driven judgment is appropriate and where fixed rules are mandatory. For example, a risk score can trigger an extra verification step, but the final access decision and its record have to stay rule-based. Design that boundary cleanly so models help without weakening security guarantees.
  • Take on team tasks and develop technical talent, with a focus on building AI engineering best practices across the team. That means AI-assisted development workflows, reusable prompt patterns, quality evaluation, and human review of AI-generated work in security-critical areas.
 

What We Look For In You

  • A security-first systems mindset. You naturally design for reliability, safe retries, consistent state, abuse prevention and complete audit trails. You know that in account security, missing an attack means a hijacked account and lost funds, while blocking a real user means lost trust, and you design with both in mind. Prior experience with identity, authentication, access management, anti-fraud or account security is a strong plus. Hands-on experience handling a real account-takeover incident or large-scale attack is an even stronger plus.
  • Solid knowledge of modern authentication and authorization standards, and their common pitfalls.

  • Hands-on experience with at least one LLM application pattern: knowledge retrieval for support and internal lookup, multi-step AI assistants for support or risk analysts, or LLM-based classification or extraction shipped to production.
  • Discipline around AI output. You don't ship AI features without proper evaluation, accuracy and abuse testing, regression checks, and human review for high-stakes actions such as account recovery or unfreezing. You have an opinion on when to use a large general-purpose model, a smaller specialized model or a simple rule, and you can defend that choice to Security and Audit.

Design task planning chains (ReAct / Plan-and-Execute), fallback and error recovery mechanisms, and result validation frameworks that accelerate the path from PoC to production.
  3. Openclaw Platform Development & Evolution: Contribute deeply to the architectural evolution and performance optimization of the Openclaw Agent Runtime. Design the plugin ecosystem, capability registry, and multi-agent orchestration mechanisms to reduce onboarding friction for product teams and improve platform extensibility and reusability.

Why Join Us
 
At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment. Our benefits include:

About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Senior Compliance Manager to build and run our global derivatives trade and transaction reporting function. The function covers CFTC swap data reporting under Part 45, EU transaction reporting under MiFIR, EU derivatives reporting under EMIR, UK MiFIR and UK EMIR, and ASIC derivative transaction reporting across multiple OKX entities and a growing derivatives product set. These regimes have different scopes, reporting parties, data requirements and destinations. You will determine how they apply to OKX’s activities and help build a reliable process for meeting each obligation.
 
Most of the work is data and judgment: deciding what is reportable, by which entity, and to whom, then making sure the right trade and lifecycle data reaches the right swap data repository, trade repository, or regulator on time and reconciles to our trading records. You will own reporting scoping/eligibility, submission monitoring, and the controls that show our reports are complete, accurate, and timely.
 
This is a hands-on Compliance leadership role. You will work with Trading, Product, Engineering, Data, Legal, local Compliance teams and reporting providers, and you will lead regulatory change in this space. Responsibilities for source data, systems, submissions and remediation will be agreed across those teams; you will lead the compliance framework and stay close enough to the process to identify and proactively resolve problems. You will report to the Head of Markets and Product Compliance and support a central function that owns reporting interpretation, scoping, oversight, and remediation for every entity in scope.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Interpret and apply derivatives and transaction reporting rules across global regimes, including CFTC Part 45, MiFIR Article 26, EMIR Article 9, UK MiFIR, UK EMIR, and the ASIC Derivative Transaction Rules (Reporting) 2024, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and outside counsel.
  • Own and maintain entity, product, and transaction-level reporting scoping and eligibility: which entity reports, which products and lifecycle events are in scope, which counterparty role triggers the obligation, and which repository or authority receives the report.

  • Reconcile reported activity to trading records and repository data, and coordinate corrections and back-reporting with the teams that own the relevant systems and data.
  • Define and maintain the reporting data specification with Engineering and Data, including field-level mapping, reference data such as LEIs, UTIs, UPIs, and ISINs, and the validation rules applied before submission.
  • Build and run the control framework: completeness, accuracy, and timeliness checks, exception management, management information, and records that hold up to regulator and audit review.
  • Drive reporting readiness and remediation. Assess new derivatives products, new entities, and regulatory changes, identify control gaps, agree on owners and deadlines across Compliance, Operations, Product, and Engineering, and track delivery.
  • Escalate material issues. Assess the impact of reporting errors, escalate to senior management, and support notifications to regulators where required.
  • Manage relationships with swap data repositories, trade repositories, approved reporting mechanisms, and reporting vendors, including onboarding, testing, and service issues.
  • Hands-on leader. Build a small team, and coordinate with and train local compliance leads.

  • A sound understanding of derivatives trade lifecycles and the data needed to report executions, changes, terminations and, where applicable, valuations and collateral.
  • The ability to interrogate large datasets, investigate reporting breaks and explain clear requirements to engineers and other business partners. SQL or comparable data analysis skills are highly desirable.
  • Experience building or improving a reporting framework, including procedures, reconciliations, exception management and evidence that can withstand regulatory or audit scrutiny; this may include remediating historical reporting errors, including back-reporting.
  • The judgment to make proportionate risk decisions, escalate material issues and lead delivery across teams without relying on a single team to own every part of the reporting process.
  • Experience with digital asset derivatives, such as perpetual futures and options, and how they map to reporting product classifications

Nice to Haves

  • Experience leading a regulatory reporting change program, such as EMIR Refit, UK EMIR Refit, the CFTC reporting rewrite, or the ASIC 2024 rules.
  • Familiarity with ISO 20022 XML reporting formats.
  • Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks.

You will build and harden the core of the Injective chain, making sure every module, upgrade and integration is safe before it reaches mainnet. You'll work alongside protocol engineers from spec to release, reviewing designs for attack vectors, auditing native chain code and EVM contracts, and building the tooling that keeps the chain secure over time. We're looking for someone who can work autonomously, has a hacker mentality, and thinks like an attacker while building like an engineer.

If you're an autonomous engineer with a strong security mindset who enjoys working with a high degree of ownership, and you're looking to protect and strengthen the financial infrastructure of one of the fastest growing blockchains, this role is for you.

  • Execute internal security audits of Injective's Cosmos-SDK modules, including the decentralized orderbook, trade execution coordinator, order matcher, and Layer-2 execution environment

Our platform processes transactions for banks and fintechs around the clock and it has run at 99.997% uptime since 2022 with zero breaches. That record is the product. We're opening our first internships in the Formal Methods group of our OCaml Language team, which develops language features and tooling for correctness reasoning and bug finding in OCaml programs. You'll also be able to attend guest speakers and social events, and hopefully get a real sense of what it would be like to work here full-time.

What’s different at Jane Street is that we aren't stuck designing verification tools for legacy languages: we can modify and improve OxCaml, our branch of OCaml, and its development environment to make them well-suited for proof-driven software development.
